Video Tutorial is available Achievements video Achievements are defined in the Developer Portal (Game Services > Achievements). An achievement is either unlocked by your game directly, or automatically by EOS when one or more Stats reach a threshold. EOS Achievements documentation
A logged in user with a Product User Id (Connect login), see Authentication The Achievements feature allowed in your client policy

Node Use EOS_Achievements_QueryDefinitions Downloads all achievement definitions (names, descriptions, icons, thresholds) EOS_Achievements_GetAchievementDefinitionCount + EOS_Achievements_CopyAchievementDefinitionV2ByIndex Reads the downloaded definitions EOS_Achievements_QueryPlayerAchievements Downloads the progress and unlock state for a player EOS_Achievements_GetPlayerAchievementCount + EOS_Achievements_CopyPlayerAchievementByIndex Reads the player's achievements EOS_Achievements_UnlockAchievements Unlocks one or more achievements by id EOS_Achievements_AddNotifyAchievementsUnlockedV2 Called when an achievement was unlocked, also for stat based unlocks

After login, call QueryDefinitions once and cache the result. Call QueryPlayerAchievements for the local player to show progress. Unlock achievements with UnlockAchievements, or ingest the stats they depend on with EOS_Stats_IngestStat. Listen to AddNotifyAchievementsUnlockedV2 to show a notification in game. tip Stat based achievements are not unlocked right away. EOS processes ingested stats on the backend, the unlock can take a few seconds.
The UnlockAchievement event unlocks ACH_FIRST_WIN for the local player. Achievement Ids is an array, so you can unlock several achievements in one call.

Call BindAchievementNotifications once after login, for example from the Game Instance. EOS_Achievements_AddNotifyAchievementsUnlockedV2 then calls OnAchievementUnlocked for every unlock, both for achievements you unlock yourself and for stat based achievements that EOS unlocks on the backend. Keep the returned Notification Id if you want to remove the notification later with EOS_Achievements_RemoveNotifyAchievementsUnlocked.

The QueryPlayerAchievements event downloads the achievements of the local player and prints the id and progress of each one: EOS_Achievements_QueryPlayerAchievements downloads the progress. Use the same id for Local User Id and Target User Id to read your own achievements. EOS_Achievements_GetPlayerAchievementCount returns the number of achievements. The For Loop reads each one with EOS_Achievements_CopyPlayerAchievementByIndex. Progress goes from 0 to 1, and Unlock Time is set when the achievement is unlocked.
The EOSCore Online Subsystem also implements IOnlineAchievements, so the engine's Write Achievement Progress and Cache Achievements nodes work as well.

Video Tutorials are available Cheaters video and Reporting Cheaters video EOS Anti-Cheat protects the game client and lets the server check that clients are protected. The game must be started through the Anti-Cheat launcher with a protected build, see the EOS documentation for how to set this up. EOS Anti-Cheat documentation warning Anti-Cheat needs an external account. A DeviceId login is not enough, see DeviceId.

Use this mode with a dedicated or listen server. Server (AntiCheatServer nodes): EOS_AntiCheatServer_AddNotifyMessageToClient: send the message to that client over your own network channel (for example a reliable RPC) EOS_AntiCheatServer_AddNotifyClientActionRequired: kick the client when EOS asks for it EOS_AntiCheatServer_BeginSession when the server starts EOS_AntiCheatServer_RegisterClient for each connecting player, EOS_AntiCheatServer_UnregisterClient when they leave EOS_AntiCheatServer_ReceiveMessageFromClient for each anti-cheat message from a client EOS_AntiCheatServer_EndSession when the server stops Client (AntiCheatClient nodes): EOS_AntiCheatClient_AddNotifyMessageToServer: send the message to the server over your own network channel EOS_AntiCheatClient_BeginSession in client-server mode when you connect, EOS_AntiCheatClient_EndSession when you leave EOS_AntiCheatClient_ReceiveMessageFromServer for each anti-cheat message from the server EOS_AntiCheatClient_AddNotifyClientIntegrityViolated: the client is not protected

Without a trusted server, every client registers the other players with EOS_AntiCheatClient_RegisterPeer, and forwards messages with EOS_AntiCheatClient_AddNotifyMessageToPeer and EOS_AntiCheatClient_ReceiveMessageFromPeer.

The server can send gameplay events to the Anti-Cheat backend for analysis, for example EOS_AntiCheatServer_LogPlayerSpawn, EOS_AntiCheatServer_LogPlayerTakeDamage, EOS_AntiCheatServer_LogGameRoundStart and EOS_AntiCheatServer_LogGameRoundEnd.

Players can report each other with EOS_Reports_SendPlayerBehaviorReport. Use EOS_Sanctions_QueryActivePlayerSanctions to check if a player is banned, and the Web API sanctions functions to create sanctions from a server or tool. Reports and Sanctions use the Product User Id (Connect login), and must be allowed in your client policy.

The ReportCheater event reports the player in Reported Player for cheating: Reporter User Id is the local player, from Get Current Product Id. Reported User Id is the Product User Id of the other player, for example from the lobby or session members. Report Category is the reason, here EOS PRC Cheating. Message is optional text from the player, and Context is optional JSON your tools can read.

The CheckSanctions event lists the active sanctions of the player in Target Player, for example when a player joins your server: EOS_Sanctions_QueryActivePlayerSanctions downloads the active sanctions of Target User Id. When the query succeeds, EOS_Sanctions_GetPlayerSanctionCount returns the number of sanctions, and the For Loop reads each one with EOS_Sanctions_CopyPlayerSanctionByIndex. Action is the action string the sanction was created with. Kick or block the player when it is one your game treats as a ban.

EOSCore has simple text chat nodes that send messages straight to another player over EOS P2P. They don't need a server, a session or a lobby, only the Product User Id of the other player. This is an EOSCore feature, not an EOS interface, so there is no client policy setting for it. For voice chat, see Voice Chat.
A logged in user with a Product User Id (Connect login) The P2P feature allowed in your client policy

Node Use Listen for Chat Messages Starts receiving messages for a local user, and calls the callback for each message Send Chat Message Sends a message to another player Clear All Chat Listeners Stops receiving messages

Call ListenForChat once after login. Listen for Chat Messages accepts chat connections from other players and calls OnChatMessage for every message, with the Sender, the Receiver and the Message. Both players must listen to receive messages. The SendChat event sends Chat Text to Chat Target. Use EOS PR Reliable Ordered for chat, so messages arrive and in the right order.

The messages use the P2P socket CHAT, so they don't interfere with your own P2P traffic or the EOSCore NetDriver. A message is sent as one P2P packet, so keep messages short (a P2P packet holds up to 1170 bytes). The sender's id is a Product User Id. To show a name, look it up with the Connect or User Info interface, see Player Name.

Custom Invites send an invite with your own text payload to other players, for example the id of a lobby, a party or a server address. Unlike lobby and session invites, EOS does not join anything for you: the receiver reads the payload and joins in your own code. EOS Custom Invites documentation
A logged in user with a Product User Id (Connect login), see Authentication The Custom Invites feature allowed in your client policy

Node Use EOS_CustomInvites_SetCustomInvite Sets the payload that the next invites carry EOS_CustomInvites_SendCustomInvite Sends the invite to one or more Product User Ids EOS_CustomInvites_AddNotifyCustomInviteReceived Called when an invite is received EOS_CustomInvites_AddNotifyCustomInviteAccepted Called when the player accepts an invite in the overlay or platform UI EOS_CustomInvites_AddNotifyCustomInviteRejected Called when the player rejects an invite EOS_CustomInvites_FinalizeInvite Tells EOS that you have handled an accepted invite EOS_CustomInvites_SendRequestToJoin Asks another player to invite you EOS_CustomInvites_AddNotifyRequestToJoinReceived Called when another player asks to join you EOS_CustomInvites_AcceptRequestToJoin, EOS_CustomInvites_RejectRequestToJoin Answers a request to join

The SendCustomInvite event invites the player in Friend: EOS_CustomInvites_SetCustomInvite sets the Payload. Use a format your game can read back, for example lobby:<lobby id>. The payload stays set, so you only need to call this again when it changes. EOS_CustomInvites_SendCustomInvite sends the invite to every id in Target User Ids. OnCustomInviteSent is called with the result.

Call BindCustomInvites once after login, for example from the Game Instance: OnCustomInviteReceived is called for every invite. Payload is the text the sender set, and Target User Id is the sender. Show the invite in your UI, and join with the payload when the player accepts it there. OnCustomInviteAccepted is called when the player accepts the invite outside your UI, for example in the EOS overlay or a console's system UI. Join with the Payload, then call EOS_CustomInvites_FinalizeInvite with the same ids and Custom Invite Id. Set Processing Result to EOS Success when the join worked, or to an error when it did not. Keep the notification ids if you want to remove the notifications later with the matching RemoveNotify nodes.
The Ecom interface handles offers, purchases and entitlements for games sold on the Epic Games Store. It needs an Epic Account login (Auth interface), not only a Connect login. EOS Ecom documentation

Node Use EOS_Ecom_QueryOffers Downloads the offers in your catalog EOS_Ecom_GetOfferCount + EOS_Ecom_CopyOfferByIndex Reads offers (title, price, currency) EOS_Ecom_Checkout Opens the purchase flow in the EOS overlay EOS_Ecom_GetTransactionCount + EOS_Ecom_CopyTransactionByIndex Reads finished transactions, release them with EOS_Ecom_Transaction_Release EOS_Ecom_QueryEntitlements Downloads what the player owns EOS_Ecom_GetEntitlementsCount + EOS_Ecom_CopyEntitlementByIndex Reads entitlements EOS_Ecom_QueryOwnership Checks if the player owns specific catalog items, for example DLC EOS_Ecom_RedeemEntitlements Marks consumable entitlements as redeemed EOS_Ecom_QueryOwnershipToken / EOS_Ecom_QueryEntitlementToken Signed tokens your backend can verify

The QueryOffers event downloads the offers in your catalog and prints the title and id of each one: Get Current Account Id gives the Epic Account Id of the logged in player. Ecom uses the Epic Account Id, not the Product User Id. EOS_Ecom_QueryOffers downloads the offers. Leave Override Catalog Namespace empty to use the catalog of your sandbox. When the query succeeds, EOS_Ecom_GetOfferCount returns the number of offers, and the For Loop reads each one with EOS_Ecom_CopyOfferByIndex. An offer has the Id you pass to Checkout, the Title Text, the Currency Code and the prices.

The BuyOffer event opens the purchase flow in the EOS overlay for the offer in Offer Id: Make one EOSEcom Checkout Entry per offer and put them in Entries. The player can buy several offers in one checkout. EOS_Ecom_Checkout opens the overlay and calls On Callback when the player closes it. On Success, Transaction Id identifies the purchase. Fail is also called when the player cancels.

The CheckDLCOwnership event checks if the player owns the catalog item in Dlc Item Id: EOS_Ecom_QueryOwnership takes an array of Catalog Item Ids, so you can check several items in one call. Item Ownership has one entry per item. The For Each Loop compares each Ownership Status with EOS OS Owned.

Checkout uses the EOS overlay, so it only works in a Standalone or packaged game started with the overlay enabled. Grant items from the transaction or from a fresh QueryEntitlements, never from the client alone. For important items, verify an ownership or entitlement token on your server. The EOSCore Online Subsystem Store/Purchase interface is only available when the game was started from the Epic Games Launcher (-EpicPortal).

Video Tutorial is available Leaderboards video A leaderboard ranks players by one Stat. Create it in the Developer Portal (Game Services > Leaderboards) and pick the stat and the sort order. You never write to a leaderboard directly: ingest the stat and the leaderboard updates. EOS Leaderboards documentation

Node Use EOS_Leaderboards_QueryLeaderboardDefinitions Downloads the leaderboard definitions EOS_Leaderboards_GetLeaderboardDefinitionCount + EOS_Leaderboards_CopyLeaderboardDefinitionByIndex Reads the definitions EOS_Leaderboards_QueryLeaderboardRanks Downloads the top ranks of a leaderboard EOS_Leaderboards_GetLeaderboardRecordCount + EOS_Leaderboards_CopyLeaderboardRecordByIndex Reads the ranks (rank, score, user id, display name) EOS_Leaderboards_CopyLeaderboardRecordByUserId Finds one player in the downloaded ranks EOS_Leaderboards_QueryLeaderboardUserScores Downloads the scores of specific players, for example friends EOS_Leaderboards_GetLeaderboardUserScoreCount + EOS_Leaderboards_CopyLeaderboardUserScoreByIndex Reads those scores

Ingest the stat with EOS_Stats_IngestStat when the match ends. Call QueryLeaderboardRanks with the leaderboard id. Loop over GetLeaderboardRecordCount and CopyLeaderboardRecordByIndex to fill your UI.

The QueryLeaderboard event downloads the top ranks of the HIGHSCORE leaderboard and prints them as 1. PlayerName - 1500: EOS_Leaderboards_QueryLeaderboardRanks downloads the ranks. Leaderboard Id is the id from the Developer Portal. When the query succeeds, EOS_Leaderboards_GetLeaderboardRecordCount returns the number of downloaded records. The For Loop reads each record with EOS_Leaderboards_CopyLeaderboardRecordByIndex. A record has the Rank, Score, User Id and User Display Name of a player. tip A leaderboard only changes when its stat is ingested, see Stats. The new score can take a short while to show up in the ranks.
The EOSCore Online Subsystem also implements IOnlineLeaderboards, so the engine's Read Leaderboard Integer and Write Leaderboard Integer nodes work as well.

A lobby is a group of players that share attributes and can talk with voice (RTC) before or during a match. Lobbies are separate from game sessions: a common setup is to gather players in a lobby, then move them to a game session, see Lobby to Session. EOS Lobbies documentation
A logged in user with a Product User Id (Connect login) The Lobbies feature allowed in your client policy Enable RTC in Project Settings if you use lobby voice

Node Use EOS_Lobby_CreateLobby Creates a lobby, you become the owner. Options include max members, permission level, presence, RTC room and host migration EOS_Lobby_CreateLobbySearch Creates a search handle EOS_LobbySearch_SetParameterString / Bool / Int64 / Double, EOS_LobbySearch_SetLobbyId, EOS_LobbySearch_SetTargetUserId Search filters EOS_LobbySearch_Find Runs the search EOS_LobbySearch_GetSearchResultCount + EOS_LobbySearch_CopySearchResultByIndex Gets a lobby details handle per result EOS_Lobby_JoinLobby / EOS_Lobby_JoinLobbyById Joins with a details handle or by lobby id EOS_Lobby_LeaveLobby / EOS_Lobby_DestroyLobby Leaves, or (owner) destroys the lobby Release every details handle (EOS_LobbyDetails_Release) and search handle (EOS_LobbySearch_Release) when you are done with it.

Node Use EOS_Lobby_UpdateLobbyModification Creates a modification handle (owner for lobby attributes, any member for member attributes) EOS_LobbyModification_AddAttribute*, EOS_LobbyModification_AddMemberAttribute*, EOS_LobbyModification_RemoveAttribute Changes attributes EOS_LobbyModification_SetMaxMembers, SetPermissionLevel, SetInvitesAllowed, SetBucketId Changes lobby settings EOS_Lobby_UpdateLobby Sends the modification EOS_LobbyDetails_CopyAttributeByKey, EOS_LobbyDetails_CopyMemberAttributeByKey Reads attributes Get Lobby Attribute String / Int64 / Double Reads the value of an attribute you copied caution EOS stores attribute keys in upper case. A key added as GameMode comes back as GAMEMODE, so use upper case keys everywhere, in searches and in CopyAttributeByKey.

Bind these once, for example in the Game Instance: EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyLobbyUpdateReceived: lobby attributes changed EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyLobbyMemberUpdateReceived: a member's attributes changed EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyLobbyMemberStatusReceived: a member joined, left, was kicked or promoted, or the lobby closed EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyLobbyInviteReceived / EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyLobbyInviteAccepted: invites EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyJoinLobbyAccepted: the player pressed Join in the social overlay, see Join Friends Lobby
EOS_Lobby_KickMember, EOS_Lobby_PromoteMember and EOS_Lobby_HardMuteMember are only allowed for the lobby owner. If host migration is enabled, EOS picks a new owner when the owner leaves.

With bEnableRTCRoom set when creating the lobby, every member joins the lobby's voice room automatically. Use EOS_Lobby_GetRTCRoomName to get the room for the RTC Audio nodes (mute, volume) and EOS_Lobby_AddNotifyRTCRoomConnectionChanged to see when voice connects.

The CreateLobby event creates a public lobby for 4 players and adds a GAMEMODE attribute that other players can search for: EOS_Lobby_CreateLobby creates the lobby. Permission Level EOS_LPL_PUBLICADVERTISED makes it visible in searches. Bucket Id groups lobbies, for example per game mode or region. When the lobby is created, EOS_Lobby_UpdateLobbyModification opens a modification handle for the new Lobby Id. EOS_LobbyModification_AddAttributeString adds GAMEMODE = Deathmatch with public visibility. EOS_Lobby_UpdateLobby sends the change. Release the handle with EOS_LobbyModification_Release when it is done. You can add several attributes to the same modification before you call UpdateLobby.

The FindAndJoinLobby event searches for a Deathmatch lobby and joins the first result: EOS_Lobby_CreateLobbySearch creates a search handle for up to 10 results. EOS_LobbySearch_SetParameterString filters on GAMEMODE equal to Deathmatch. EOS_LobbySearch_Find runs the search. EOS_LobbySearch_GetSearchResultCount returns how many lobbies were found. If at least one lobby was found, EOS_LobbySearch_CopySearchResultByIndex gives a lobby details handle for the first one and EOS_Lobby_JoinLobby joins it. Release the details handle and the search handle when you are done with them, also when nothing was found.

Call BindLobbyNotifications once, for example from the Game Instance: OnLobbyMemberStatus runs when a member joins, leaves, is kicked or promoted, or when the lobby is closed. Current Status says which. OnLobbyUpdated runs when the owner changes the lobby. The example copies a lobby details handle for the Lobby Id, reads the GAMEMODE attribute with EOS_LobbyDetails_CopyAttributeByKey and Get Lobby Attribute String, and releases the handle again.

The LeaveLobby event leaves the lobby with the given Lobby Id. The owner can use EOS_Lobby_DestroyLobby instead, which closes the lobby for all members. note If the owner destroys the lobby while you are leaving, EOS_Lobby_LeaveLobby returns EOS_NotFound. The lobby is already gone, so treat it as a successful leave.

The Metrics interface records when a player starts and stops playing. EOS uses it for the player and session statistics in the Developer Portal, such as daily active users and play time. EOS Metrics documentation
Node Use EOS_Metrics_BeginPlayerSession The player started playing EOS_Metrics_EndPlayerSession The player stopped playing

Call BeginMetricsSession after login. Account Id Type says which id identifies the player: EOS MAIT Epic uses the Epic Account Id in Epic, and EOS MAIT External uses the text in External, for example a Steam id or a DeviceId login. Display Name is the name shown for the player. Controller Type, Server Ip and Game Session Id are optional and let you split the statistics by input device and game session. Call EndMetricsSession with the same Account Id Type and id when the player leaves the game or logs out. tip Begin a new player session for every login, and always end it, also when the player returns to the main menu and logs in with another account.

The Mods interface lists, installs, updates and uninstalls mods that are published for your game on the Epic Games Store. It needs an Epic Account login (Auth interface), and the game must be started from the Epic Games Launcher, which installs the mods. EOS Mods documentation

Node Use EOS_Mods_EnumerateMods Downloads the list of installed mods, or of all mods available to the player EOS_Mods_CopyModInfo Reads the list from the last EnumerateMods EOS_Mods_InstallMod Installs a mod EOS_Mods_UpdateMod Updates an installed mod EOS_Mods_UninstallMod Uninstalls a mod The Mods nodes need a target: connect Get Mods.

The ListInstalledMods event calls EOS_Mods_EnumerateMods with Type set to EOS MET INSTALLED. Use EOS MET ALL AVAILABLE to list every mod the player can install. OnModsEnumerated is called when the list is ready. EOS_Mods_CopyModInfo reads it, with the same Type. The For Each Loop prints the Title and Version of each mod. Pass the whole EOSMod Identifier to InstallMod, UpdateMod or UninstallMod.

The P2P interface sends packets directly between players, with NAT traversal and Epic relay servers when a direct connection is not possible. Players are addressed by their Product User Id, no IP addresses or open ports are needed. EOS P2P documentation tip For normal Unreal replication you don't need these nodes. The EOSCore NetDriver uses P2P for you, see Configuring Online Subsystem. Use the P2P nodes for your own messages, for example chat or a lobby handshake.

Node Use EOS_P2P_SendPacket Sends data to a remote user on a socket name and channel. The first packet opens the connection EOS_P2P_AddNotifyPeerConnectionRequest Called when a remote user wants to connect EOS_P2P_AcceptConnection Accepts the connection (call it for incoming requests, or before you send to open both ways) EOS_P2P_GetNextReceivedPacketSize + EOS_P2P_ReceivePacket Reads received packets, call it every tick EOS_P2P_CloseConnection / EOS_P2P_CloseConnections Closes one or all connections on a socket EOS_P2P_AddNotifyPeerConnectionEstablished / Interrupted / Closed Connection state changes

Node Use EOS_P2P_QueryNATType + EOS_P2P_GetNATType Finds the local NAT type EOS_P2P_SetRelayControl / EOS_P2P_GetRelayControl Allows, forces or forbids relay servers. Forcing relays hides player IP addresses from each other EOS_P2P_SetPortRange / EOS_P2P_GetPortRange Limits the local UDP ports EOS_P2P_SetPacketQueueSize + EOS_P2P_AddNotifyIncomingPacketQueueFull Limits the packet queues
The example sends text messages between two players on a socket named CHAT. Both players run the same Blueprint.

Call StartP2P once after login. EOS_P2P_AddNotifyPeerConnectionRequest calls OnP2PConnectionRequest when another player sends the first packet on the CHAT socket. The event accepts the connection with EOS_P2P_AcceptConnection, using the user ids and socket from the request.

SendChatMessage takes the Remote User Id of the other player and the text to send. Core String To Byte turns the text into bytes and EOS_P2P_SendPacket sends them on channel 1 with Reliability EOS_PR_ReliableOrdered, so messages arrive and arrive in order. Channels go from 0 to 255 and let you keep different kinds of messages apart on the same socket. The remote user id is the Product User Id of the other player, for example from a lobby member or a session.

Packets are queued until you read them, so call ReceivePackets every tick or from a looping timer: EOS_P2P_GetNextReceivedPacketSize returns EOS_Success and the size when a packet is waiting, and EOS_NotFound when the queue is empty. Requested Channel -1 reads from any channel, set it to a channel number to read only that channel. EOS_P2P_ReceivePacket reads the packet. Max Data Size Bytes is the size from step 1. Core Bytes To String turns the data back into text. Out Peer Id says who sent it. To read every waiting packet in one tick, repeat the two calls until GetNextReceivedPacketSize no longer returns EOS_Success.

The Progression Snapshot interface stores a snapshot of a player's progression on the EOS backend, as a list of key/value text pairs, for example the player's level, character and chapter. EOS uses the snapshots when a player merges several Epic accounts into one: the player sees the progression of each account and picks the one to keep. EOS Progression Snapshot documentation
A logged in user with a Product User Id (Connect login)

Node Use EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_BeginSnapshot Starts a new snapshot and returns its Snapshot Id EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_AddProgression Adds one key/value pair to the snapshot EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_SubmitSnapshot Sends the snapshot to the backend EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_EndSnapshot Frees the local snapshot EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_DeleteSnapshot Deletes the stored snapshots of the player

The SaveProgressionSnapshot event stores the player's level: EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_BeginSnapshot starts a snapshot for the Product User Id and returns the Out Snapshot Id the other nodes use. EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_AddProgression adds level with the value of Level. Call it once for every key. Keys and values are text, so convert numbers to strings. EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_SubmitSnapshot sends all pairs, and OnSnapshotSubmitted is called with the result. EOS_ProgressionSnapshot_EndSnapshot frees the snapshot. You can call it right after Submit. A new snapshot replaces the previous one, so always add all keys, not only the ones that changed.

These interfaces use Epic Account Services and need an Epic Account login (Auth interface) with the matching permissions (scopes), see Scope Consent. EOS Friends documentation EOS Presence documentation EOS User Info documentation note The EOSCore Online Subsystem also implements IOnlineFriends, IOnlinePresence, IOnlineUser and parts of IOnlineExternalUI (login, friends overlay, web URL), so C++ code and plugins that use the Online Subsystem can use them as well. In Blueprints, use the EOSCore nodes below. See Supported Platforms and Features.

Node Use EOS_Friends_QueryFriends Downloads the friends list (needs the Friends List scope) EOS_Friends_GetFriendsCount + EOS_Friends_GetFriendAtIndex Reads the friends' Epic Account Ids EOS_Friends_GetStatus Friend, invite sent, invite received or not friends EOS_Friends_SendInvite, EOS_Friends_AcceptInvite, EOS_Friends_RejectInvite Friend invites EOS_Friends_AddNotifyFriendsUpdate Called when the friends list changes

The QueryFriends event downloads the friends list of the local player and prints each friend: EOS_Friends_QueryFriends downloads the list for the Epic Account Id from Get Current Account Id. When the query succeeds, EOS_Friends_GetFriendsCount returns the number of friends, and the For Loop reads each one with EOS_Friends_GetFriendAtIndex. EOSEpic Account Id to String turns the id into text. To show the friend's name, query it with EOS_UserInfo_QueryUserInfo, see Player Name.

Call BindFriendsNotifications once after login. EOS_Friends_AddNotifyFriendsUpdate then calls OnFriendsUpdate every time the status of a friend changes, for example when an invite is sent, received or accepted. Previous Status and Current Status tell you what changed. In this example, a new friend is printed when Current Status becomes EOS FS Friends. Keep the returned notification id if you want to remove the notification later.

Node Use EOS_Presence_CreatePresenceModification Creates a modification handle EOS_PresenceModification_SetStatus, SetRawRichText, SetData, SetJoinInfo Online status, rich text ("In a match"), key/value data and the join info friends use to join you EOS_Presence_SetPresence Sends the modification, then EOS_PresenceModification_Release EOS_Presence_QueryPresence + EOS_Presence_CopyPresence Reads a friend's presence EOS_Presence_AddNotifyOnPresenceChanged Called when a friend's presence changes EOS_Presence_AddNotifyJoinGameAccepted The player pressed Join on a friend in the social overlay, see Join Friends Game

The SetInMatchPresence event shows "In a match" next to the player's name in the friends list: EOS_Presence_CreatePresenceModification creates a handle that collects the changes. EOS_PresenceModification_SetStatus sets the online status, and EOS_PresenceModification_SetRawRichText sets the text. Use SetData and SetJoinInfo on the same handle for key/value data and join info. EOS_Presence_SetPresence sends all changes at once. Release the handle with EOS_PresenceModification_Release when the call is done.

Node Use EOS_UserInfo_QueryUserInfo Downloads a user's account info EOS_UserInfo_CopyUserInfo Display name, country, language EOS_UserInfo_CopyBestDisplayName The name to show for a player, also for players from other platforms EOS_UserInfo_QueryUserInfoByDisplayName Finds a user by display name See Player Name for an example.

Video Tutorial is available Stats video Stats are numeric values per player (kills, wins, playtime) that EOS aggregates on the backend. Define them in the Developer Portal (Game Services > Stats) with an aggregation type (SUM, LATEST, MIN or MAX). Leaderboards and stat based Achievements are built on stats. EOS Stats documentation
A logged in user with a Product User Id (Connect login) The Stats feature allowed in your client policy

Node Use EOS_Stats_IngestStat Sends one or more stat values. The backend aggregates them with the stat's aggregation type EOS_Stats_QueryStats Downloads the stats of a player EOS_Stats_GetStatsCount + EOS_Stats_CopyStatByIndex Reads the downloaded stats EOS_Stats_CopyStatByName Reads one downloaded stat by name

Ingested values are added to the aggregation, they don't replace the stat (except LATEST). Ingest the change (for example Kills = 1), not the total. Stats are not updated immediately. Query them again after a short delay if you need the new value.

The IngestKills event adds 1 to the KILLS stat of the local player: Get Current Product Id gives the Product User Id of the logged in player. Use it as both Local User Id and Target User Id. Make one EOSStats Ingest Data per stat. Stat Name is the stat id from the Developer Portal, Ingest Amount is the change. EOS_Stats_IngestStat sends the array. EOS Success splits the result code into Success and Fail. You can send several stats in one call by adding more pins to Make Array.

The QueryStats event downloads the stats of the local player and prints each one: EOS_Stats_QueryStats downloads the stats. Leave Stat Names empty to get all stats, or add names to download only those. When the query succeeds, EOS_Stats_GetStatsCount returns how many stats were downloaded. The For Loop runs from 0 to count - 1 and EOS_Stats_CopyStatByIndex reads each stat. Name and Value are printed. Use EOS_Stats_CopyStatByName instead of the loop when you only need one stat.
The EOSCore Online Subsystem also implements IOnlineStats (UpdateStats, QueryStats).

EOS has two file services: Title Storage Player Data Storage Who writes You, in the Developer Portal The player, from the game Who reads All players Only that player Typical use Patch notes, configuration, news Save games, settings Both encrypt files with the Encryption Key of your configuration, see Project Settings. Changing the key makes existing files unreadable. EOS Title Storage documentation EOS Player Data Storage documentation
documents.s: Title Storage and Player Data Storage

documents.t: Node Use EOS_TitleStorage_QueryFileList Lists files with the given tags EOS_TitleStorage_GetFileMetadataCount + EOS_TitleStorage_CopyFileMetadataAtIndex Reads file names, sizes and hashes EOS_TitleStorage_QueryFile / EOS_TitleStorage_CopyFileMetadataByFilename Metadata of one file EOS_TitleStorage_ReadFile Downloads a file to a local file, with progress EOS_TitleStorage_DeleteCache Clears the local cache Files are uploaded in the Developer Portal under Game Services > Title Storage, with tags used by QueryFileList.

See the step by step SaveGames example. Use WriteFile to upload a local file and ReadFile to download it. Use an absolute path for the local file. Run one read and one write at a time. Wait for the completion callback before you start the next transfer of the same kind. Files are limited in size and count per player, see the EOS documentation for the current limits.

The UploadSaveGame event uploads Saved/SaveGames/Slot1.sav, the file the engine writes for Save Game to Slot with the slot name Slot1: Get Project Saved Directory plus SaveGames/Slot1.sav gives the absolute path of the local file. Remote File is the name of the file in the cloud. EOS_PlayerDataStorage_WriteFile uploads the file. The result is printed with EOS Result To String.
The DownloadSaveGame event downloads Slot1.sav again and writes it to the same local path. After a successful download you can load it with Load Game from Slot.

The ListPlayerFiles event prints the name of every file the player has uploaded: EOS_PlayerDataStorage_QueryFileList downloads the file list. EOS_PlayerDataStorage_GetFileMetadataCount returns the number of files. The For Loop reads each file with EOS_PlayerDataStorage_CopyFileMetadataAtIndex. The metadata also has the size, the MD5 hash and the last modified time.

The DownloadTitleFile event downloads Config.json, a file you uploaded in the Developer Portal, to Saved/TitleStorage/Config.json. Filename is the name in Title Storage and Save File Name is the absolute local path. Title Storage files are read only for the game.

The UI interface controls the EOS overlay: the social overlay with the friends list, and the dialogs to block or report a player. The overlay needs an Epic Account login (Auth interface). EOS UI documentation note The overlay is only drawn in a Standalone or packaged game, not in Play In Editor. The player can also open it with the toggle key, Shift+F3 by default.

Node Use EOS_UI_ShowFriends, EOS_UI_HideFriends Opens or closes the friends list in the overlay EOS_UI_GetFriendsVisible True while the friends list is open EOS_UI_SetToggleFriendsKey, EOS_UI_GetToggleFriendsKey The key combination that opens the friends list EOS_UI_SetToggleFriendsButton, EOS_UI_GetToggleFriendsButton The gamepad button combination that opens the friends list EOS_UI_SetDisplayPreference Where on screen the overlay shows notifications EOS_UI_AddNotifyDisplaySettingsUpdated Called when the overlay opens or closes EOS_UI_ShowBlockPlayer, EOS_UI_ShowReportPlayer Opens the dialog to block or report a player EOS_UI_PauseSocialOverlay, EOS_UI_IsSocialOverlayPaused Stops the overlay from opening, for example during a cutscene

The ShowFriendsOverlay event opens the friends list for the player from Get Current Account Id. On Callback is called when the overlay has opened, or with an error when it could not. Call BindOverlayNotifications once after login. EOS_UI_AddNotifyDisplaySettingsUpdated then calls OnOverlayDisplayChanged every time the overlay opens or closes. Is Visible is true while the overlay is shown, and Is Exclusive Input is true while it takes all input. Pause your game input or open your pause menu while it is visible. See Join Friends Game and Join Friends Lobby for what happens when a player presses Join in the overlay.

To enable Multiplayer on an Android device you must edit the AndroidEngine.ini configuration file, this is the Android equivalent to DefaultEngine.ini, copy-paste the settings from the DefaultEngine.ini to your AndroidEngine.ini (see the example below). This example will allow you to connect using the EOS NAT P2P Interface and enable cross-platform multiplayer.

NOTE Double check the location of your AndroidEngine.ini configuration file, it must be located in Config\Android\AndroidEngine.ini AndroidEngine.ini [OnlineSubsystem] DefaultPlatformService=EOSCore [/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.NetDriverEOSCore] NetConnectionClassName=/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.NetConnectionEOSCore bIsUsingP2PSockets=true [/Script/Engine.GameEngine] !NetDriverDefinitions=ClearArray +NetDriverDefinitions=(DefName="GameNetDriver",DriverClassName="/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.NetDriverEOSCore",DriverClassNameFallback="/Script/OnlineSubsystemUtils.IpNetDriver")

Using EOS on android requires an additional step, we need to set the Android Client Id in Project Setting. The Client Id we use for our android device can be the same used throughout our entire project, but Android devices requires this additional step because of login intent callback.
If you’re going to use multiplayer features on your Android Device, you also need to configure the AndroidEngine.ini configuration file, see Android Multiplayer for an example on how to set this up.

To enable Multiplayer on an iOS device you must edit the IOSEngine.ini configuration file, this is the IOS equivalent to DefaultEngine.ini, copy-paste the settings from the DefaultEngine.ini to your IOSEngine.ini (see the example below). This example will allow you to connect using the EOS NAT P2P Interface and enable cross-platform multiplayer.

NOTE Double check the location of your IOSEngine.ini configuration file, it must be located in Config\IOS\IOSEngine.ini IOSEngine.ini [OnlineSubsystem] DefaultPlatformService=EOSCore [/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.NetDriverEOSCore] NetConnectionClassName=/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.NetConnectionEOSCore bIsUsingP2PSockets=true [/Script/Engine.GameEngine] !NetDriverDefinitions=ClearArray +NetDriverDefinitions=(DefName="GameNetDriver",DriverClassName="/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.NetDriverEOSCore",DriverClassNameFallback="/Script/OnlineSubsystemUtils.IpNetDriver")

You can now use EOSCore on your IOS devices! All you have to do is configure the IOS Client Id, this can be the same Client Id for all of your other clients but this has to be set manually as well, you can set it in the “Project Settings > EOSCore Plugin“. The plugin will handle the rest.
TIP This Example has a Video Tutorial that you can find here: Related Video

You must host your dedicated game server on a remote machine/pc for everything to work correctly, firewalls and routers also has to be configured to allow UDP port 7777 (the default game port, or the port you pass with -Port=) for clients to connect successfully. If you are hosting the server on the same PC you’re connecting from it will not work as expected because of how network routing works, please use a correct server setup as described above.
Since Dedicated Servers don’t use Relay Servers we have to disable the EOSCoreNetDriver, simply removing the declarations will disable using the EOS NetDriver.

Here is an example of what your DefaultEngine.ini should look like [Core.Log] Online=Verbose OnlineSession=Verbose OnlineGame=Verbose LogEOSCoreSubsystem=Verbose LogEOSCore=Verbose [OnlineSubsystem] DefaultPlatformService=EOSCore [/Script/Engine.GameEngine] !NetDriverDefinitions=ClearArray +NetDriverDefinitions=(DefName="GameNetDriver",DriverClassName="/Script/OnlineSubsystemUtils.IpNetDriver",DriverClassNameFallback="/Script/OnlineSubsystemUtils.IpNetDriver") [/Script/OnlineSubsystemUtils.IpNetDriver] MaxClientRate=1000000000 MaxInternetClientRate=1000000000 InitialConnectTimeout=120.0 [EOSSDK] bHasProjectBinary=true

We’ll use Commandline arguments to launch our server. -EOSConfig= is optional, use it if you have a separate configuration for your server in Project Settings (for example one that uses a server client policy). -Port= sets the game port, the plugin publishes it in the session so clients connect to the right port. D:\WindowsServer\EOS_DedicatedServer.exe -log -Port=7777 -EOSConfig=ServerConfig note Automatic login with -AUTH_TYPE= only runs in Game and Client builds. In a build of a Server target it is ignored, so the server does not log in a user this way. If you run the server from a Game or Editor binary with -server, -AUTH_TYPE=deviceid -AUTH_LOGIN=<display name> logs the server in with a DeviceId. See Commandline Arguments for all arguments.
You can use the default Session nodes to list a Dedicated Server. We’ll use the GameInstance in this example. This will List your dedicated server as a joinable session.

To join a dedicated server there are a few things you need to take into account: If you're hosting the server on your own local network you'll not be able to join the server via a server browser, this is because the server reports your external IP address to EOS and you can't join your own local network via your external ip address. If your server is hosted on your local network use the console to connect to it (see the sample below). Make sure that your client is logged in before trying to connect to the server.
Replace 127.0.0.1 with your servers IP address open 127.0.0.1
The EOSCore plugin comes with a custom “Find EOS Sessions” node that allows you to find custom session attributes. TIP This Example has a Video Tutorial that you can find here: Related Video
You can also set a Filter value when searching for sessions, in this example you’ll only receive session results that contain the “eoscore” string.
You can also use the default “Find Sessions” node that comes with UE4 to find EOS Sessions

First we need to bind the invite accepted event, we do this in our PlayerController (in this example), like this The rest is handled by the plugin in the background, that is all you need to do to get Invites working!
You can allow your friends to join your pre-game lobby

To join a friends lobby from the Social Overlay all you have to do is to bind the event that is called when you click the “JOIN” button, In this example we're using using the PlayerController to bind this event but you can do it anywhere you want. The Callback in the above screenshot will get executed when you press the “JOIN” button in the Social Overlay screen, after that we will get the lobby Handle needed to join the lobby our friend is currently in, then it’s simply a matter of joining the lobby and releasing the handle. That’s all you need!
To enable this functionality, all you need to do is to bind this delegate and join the session. You can now join your friends from the Social Overlay!

If you use the Online Subsystem session interface instead, pressing Join in the overlay calls OnSessionUserInviteAccepted with the friend's session as the search result, the same delegate that accepted invites use. Join it with JoinSession: SessionInterface->AddOnSessionUserInviteAcceptedDelegate_Handle(FOnSessionUserInviteAcceptedDelegate::CreateLambda( [SessionInterface](bool bWasSuccessful, int32 LocalUserNum, FUniqueNetIdPtr UserId, const FOnlineSessionSearchResult& SearchResult) { if (bWasSuccessful) { SessionInterface->JoinSession(LocalUserNum, NAME_GameSession, SearchResult); } })); warning Use either the Blueprint event above or the Online Subsystem delegate. If you bind both, both are called and the player joins twice.

The EOSCore Online Subsystem can use EOS Lobbies instead of EOS Sessions behind the normal IOnlineSession interface. The same Create, Find, Join, Update, Destroy and invite functions work. They talk to the EOS Lobby interface when the session settings ask for it. Lobby sessions are meant for player hosted games, such as parties, listen servers and peer-to-peer games. Dedicated servers cannot own a lobby, so use EOS Sessions for them.

The local user is logged in with EOS Connect (a Product User Id). Players connect to the lobby owner over EOS P2P, so use the EOSCore NetDriver with bIsUsingP2PSockets=true. See Configuring Online Subsystem. Create the session before you open the level with listen. The host listens on a P2P socket named after the lobby id.

Set bUseLobbiesIfAvailable in the session settings. FOnlineSessionSettings Settings; Settings.NumPublicConnections = 4; Settings.bShouldAdvertise = true; Settings.bUsesPresence = true; Settings.bAllowJoinViaPresence = true; Settings.bAllowInvites = true; Settings.bUseLobbiesIfAvailable = true; Settings.bUseLobbiesVoiceChatIfAvailable = false; Settings.Set(SETTING_HOST_MIGRATION, true, EOnlineDataAdvertisementType::DontAdvertise); Settings.Set(FName(TEXT("GAMEMODE")), FString(TEXT("Coop")), EOnlineDataAdvertisementType::ViaOnlineService); SessionInterface->CreateSession(0, NAME_GameSession, Settings); Setting Lobby option NumPublicConnections + NumPrivateConnections Max lobby members (EOS allows up to 64) NumPublicConnections > 0 Public advertised lobby NumPublicConnections == 0 and bAllowJoinViaPresence Join via presence Otherwise Invite only bUsesPresence Lobby presence, so friends can join from the EOS overlay bAllowInvites Invites allowed bUseLobbiesVoiceChatIfAvailable Creates the lobby RTC voice room. The platform must be created with RTC enabled SETTING_HOST_MIGRATION Host migration, on by default SessionIdOverride (UE 5.1+) Custom lobby id, 4 to 32 characters Settings advertised with ViaOnlineService or ViaOnlineServiceAndPing become lobby attributes. MemberSettings for the local user become member attributes.

Set SEARCH_LOBBIES to true in the query settings. The other query settings are used as lobby search filters. SessionSearch = MakeShared<FOnlineSessionSearch>(); SessionSearch->MaxSearchResults = 50; SessionSearch->QuerySettings.Set(SEARCH_LOBBIES, true, EOnlineComparisonOp::Equals); SessionSearch->QuerySettings.Set(FName(TEXT("GAMEMODE")), FString(TEXT("Coop")), EOnlineComparisonOp::Equals); SessionInterface->FindSessions(0, SessionSearch.ToSharedRef()); FindFriendSession finds the lobby a friend is in, and FindSessionById looks for a lobby with that id first and then for an EOS session.

Join a search result with JoinSession. When OnJoinSessionComplete reports success, get the connect string and travel: FString ConnectString; if (SessionInterface->GetResolvedConnectString(NAME_GameSession, ConnectString)) { PlayerController->ClientTravel(ConnectString, TRAVEL_Absolute); } The connect string is an EOS P2P address for the lobby owner, EOS:<OwnerProductUserId>:<LobbyId>:<Channel>.

UpdateSession updates the lobby. Only the owner can change lobby settings and attributes. Other members only update their own member attributes. Lobby changes call OnSessionSettingsUpdated. Members joining and leaving call OnSessionParticipantJoined and OnSessionParticipantLeft (UE 5.2+) or OnSessionParticipantsChange (older engines). Member attribute changes call OnSessionParticipantSettingsUpdated. SendSessionInviteToFriend sends a lobby invite. Received invites call OnSessionInviteReceived. Accepted invites and Join in the EOS overlay call OnSessionUserInviteAccepted. Leave in the EOS overlay calls OnDestroySessionRequested (UE 5.5+). On older engines the session is destroyed directly. DestroySession leaves the lobby. If the owner leaves with host migration on, EOS promotes another member, and that member's session becomes the owner. If the lobby is closed or the local user is kicked, the session is removed and OnDestroySessionComplete is called.
In this example we’re going to take a look how to transition from a Lobby to a Game Session using only Blueprints and EOSCore
Creating a EOS lobby is rather simple, all you have to do is call the “Create Lobby” function, for a complete lobby setup see the EOSCore Example Project

We’re going to bind the “Lobby Update Received” delegate in the Lobby system so that we’ll get notified once the game server is available. The branch check in this example is to make sure that once the game is created the delegate will also be invoked on the host and we don’t want the host to try and connect to himself, since we’re using EOS Product Id to connect to the game session we can check if the LobbyOwner is the same as host for the game session. Then it’s simply a matter of invoking the console command “open EOS:ProductId:GameSession:97″ for the client(s) to connect to the host.

In this example we’re going to be creating a simple game session by opening a level with the “listen” parameter, you could also use the “Create EOSCore Session” node to create your session but this is not covered in this example to keep it simple and understandable. Calling the function “Update Lobby” will invoke the delegate we bound earlier on all clients that are inside the lobby, in this case we’re using the EOSCoreNetDriver so we will use our ProductId as the SERVER_ADDRESS because clients will use our ProductId when connecting to us. Then it’s simply a matter of opening the level with the “listen” parameter, also note that you should not set the lobby game server before the map has actually finished loading on the host, but for simplicity's sake we’re setting the game server first and then loading the map in this example.

This event will be called once the host updates the lobby from the delegate we bound earlier, you may want to add some checks to make sure that the attribute was found and so on, but this is a mere example to get you started, The final console command should look something like this:​ open EOS:ProductId:GameSession:97
TIP This Example has a Video Tutorial that you can find here: Related Video

You must use 2 different accounts (for example 1 DeviceId and 1 Epic Account) when testing multiplayer DeviceId can’t be used when testing multiplayer on the same machine, you can however use 1 Epic Account and 1 DeviceId Account It's recommended that you package your game project rather than using the editor. If you're testing in the editor you must use a Standalone Instance (see below)
The best way when testing multiplayer on the same machine is to use the DevTool that is provided by the EOS SDK. You can obtain the DevTool from the EOS Developer Portal, “Download SDK“

After obtaining your copy of the DevTool, launch the application and create your token. NOTE Remember that for each multiplayer instance you must use a separate Epic Account, using the same Epic account for multiple instances will not work!
When testing in the editor you must use a Standalone Game instance, however it's recommended that you use a packaged game client when testing multiplayer (and not use the editor)
EOSCore 1.9.3.6 and onwards now supports in game voice chat using the Online Subsystem.

First edit your DefaultEngine.ini configuration file and make sure it has these values configured. [Voice] bEnabled=true [OnlineSubsystem] DefaultPlatformService=EOSCore bHasVoiceEnabled=true [/Script/Engine.GameSession] bRequiresPushToTalk=true

Below is a configuration example that includes all EOSCore settings (including Voice Chat configuration) [Core.Log] LogEOSCoreSubsystem=Verbose LogEOSCore=Verbose LogEOSCoreWeb=Verbose [Voice] bEnabled=true [OnlineSubsystem] DefaultPlatformService=EOSCore bHasVoiceEnabled=true [/Script/Engine.GameSession] bRequiresPushToTalk=true
This example is going to utilize the Character and PlayerController blueprints to setup and handle VOIP.
The PlayerController is going to control the Push to Talk input.

To use custom channels we need to use a TrustedServer to Create/Generate tokens for our clients to securely join the proper channels. This tutorial will show you all the steps required to get your Voice setup.

Let’s start by creating the Voice Server Policy, click on the “Add new client policy” button in your Product Settings Give your policy a name and select “TrustedServer” policy type The only permissions we need to give the server in this demonstration is the Voice Permissions, they should be pre-selected but if they are not then select them accordingly.
Next we’re going to create our Client, click on the “Add new client” button Give your client a Name and select the Policy we created in the previous step The finished result!

This step is optional, but it’s a good idea to get the Clients Ip Address so that EOS can choose the best server for the client to connect to, GetPublicIp is a utility function provided by EOSCore Use the Credentials that we created earlier for our VOICE_SERVER, these settings should be set like in the example below when calling “RequestAccessToken“ We request our AccessToken from the Epic Web API and wait for a response, after we receive our AccessToken we can use the Token to generate a Room Token for our Client to use to join the channel The last step we finally get to join our room, see the example below:

EOSCore creates the EOS platform (EOS_HPlatform) that its Online Subsystem uses. Other plugins can use that same platform instead of creating their own, even if they can't depend on the EOSCore modules. EOSCore publishes the platform as a modular feature named EOSPlatformHandleProvider. This page is for C++ plugin authors.
documents.s: Sharing the EOS Platform with Other Plugins

documents.t: Copy this header into your plugin unchanged. The #ifndef guard lets several plugins carry their own copy. #pragma once #include "CoreMinimal.h" #include "Features/IModularFeature.h" #ifndef EOS_PLATFORM_HANDLE_PROVIDER_DEFINED #define EOS_PLATFORM_HANDLE_PROVIDER_DEFINED class IEOSPlatformHandleProvider : public IModularFeature { public: static FName GetModularFeatureName() { static const FName FeatureName(TEXT("EOSPlatformHandleProvider")); return FeatureName; } /** The EOS_HPlatform, or null while there is none. */ virtual void* GetEOSPlatformHandle() const = 0; }; #endif

#include "Features/IModularFeatures.h" #include "EOSPlatformHandleProvider.h" EOS_HPlatform GetSharedEOSPlatform() { IModularFeatures& Features = IModularFeatures::Get(); const FName Name = IEOSPlatformHandleProvider::GetModularFeatureName(); if (Features.IsModularFeatureAvailable(Name)) { IEOSPlatformHandleProvider& Provider = Features.GetModularFeature<IEOSPlatformHandleProvider>(Name); return static_cast<EOS_HPlatform>(Provider.GetEOSPlatformHandle()); } return nullptr; }

EOSCore registers the feature when the Online Subsystem initializes and unregisters it when the Online Subsystem shuts down, before it releases the platform. Don't keep the handle around. Ask the provider again when you need it, or listen to IModularFeatures::Get().OnModularFeatureUnregistered() and stop using the handle when the feature goes away. In the editor every PIE instance has its own Online Subsystem and platform, so several providers can be registered at the same time. GetModularFeature returns the first one. Don't call EOS_Platform_Release or EOS_Shutdown on the shared platform, EOSCore owns it. EOS callbacks run when the platform ticks. EOSCore ticks it, so you don't have to.
EOSCore is configured in Project Settings > Plugins > EOSCore Plugin. The settings are saved in Config/DefaultEngine.ini under the section [/Script/OnlineSubsystemEOSCore.EOSCoreSettings].

You can add several configurations, for example one for the client and one for a dedicated server. The plugin picks one when it starts: The configuration named by the -EOSConfig= command line argument, if it exists. Otherwise the configuration named by Default Configuration Name. If no configuration matches, the plugin does not initialize and the log shows GetEOSConfig(): Did not find any EOS Configuration. Start by turning on Additional Logging and read the log in your project's Saved/Logs folder. Most problems show up there as an EOS result code.

Result Usual cause Fix EOS_NotConfigured The plugin did not create an EOS platform, so every EOSCore function and async node fails right away with this result Check that your configuration in Project Settings is complete and that its name matches Default Configuration Name (or -EOSConfig=). Look for GetEOSConfig() and PlatformCreate() errors in the log EOS_InvalidUser Connect login worked, but there is no EOS user for this external account yet Call EOS_Connect_CreateUser with the ContinuanceToken from the login callback (once per account). The Login node does this for you EOS_DuplicateNotAllowed from CreateDeviceId A DeviceId already exists on this device Not an error, continue with the login EOS_AccessDenied, EOS_InvalidAuth The client policy does not allow this action, or ClientId/ClientSecret are wrong Check the client and its policy in the Developer Portal, see Client & Policy Settings EOS_InvalidParameters A required option is empty, often LocalUserId because the user is not logged in yet Log in first, see Authentication EOS_Auth_ScopeConsentRequired and other scope errors The Scope Flags in Project Settings do not match the application permissions Make them match, see Scope Consent

"Failed to load EOS third party library": the EOS SDK binary next to the plugin could not be loaded. Check that Plugins/EOSCore/Source/ThirdParty/EOSLibrary/Bin exists in your build and that no other EOS SDK version is loaded. Warnings about EOSShared, OnlineSubsystemEOS, EOSVoiceChat or SocketSubsystemEOS in the editor log: one of the engine's EOS plugins is enabled. Disable them, or add [EOSSDK] bHasProjectBinary=true, see Installing the Plugin. Nothing happens at all: check that [OnlineSubsystem] DefaultPlatformService=EOSCore is set and that bEnabled is not false, see Configuring Online Subsystem.

The Epic Account login (Account Portal) does not open: the EOS overlay only works in a Standalone Game or a packaged game, not in PIE. See Epic Account. Login works but Online Subsystem functions say the player is not logged in: when you log in with the async nodes you have to update the player's UniqueNetId yourself, see Authentication. The player is logged out after about an hour: login tokens expire, see Refreshing Tokens.

Two instances on the same computer can't see each other: both use the same DeviceId. Use two different accounts, for example two DevTool credentials, see Testing Multiplayer. Can't join a session after leaving one: the old session was not destroyed, see Leaving a Session. Can't join your own dedicated server from the server browser: the server reports its external IP. Connect with open <local ip> on your local network, see Dedicated Server.

ReadFile/WriteFile with a relative path fails: use an absolute path for the local file. Run one read and one write at a time. Starting a second transfer of the same kind before the first one has finished is not supported.

Epic Games Services uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication and authorization, supporting common-use cases for web servers and client-side applications. Epic has also introduced custom grant types for some specific use cases. Before starting, you will need to obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials from Epic. These will be in the form of a Client ID and Client Secret, and will be used when requesting an access token from the Epic authorization server. See our guide on Getting Started with Epic Account Services for more details. https://dev.epicgames.com/docs/web-api-ref/authentication https://dev.epicgames.com/portal note Note that the AccessToken in this example will not work for creating a RoomToken as that requires a TrustedServer Client. Use RequestAccessToken from the Connect category for this, see Web API. Note that this authentication flow is not supported on Mobile devices.

Before getting started we need to setup our Redirect URL, the web browser will redirect the user to this address upon successful Epic Authentication and the plugin will then use this URL to determine the Authentication Code from the user. Begin by logging into your Developer Portal and go to your Product Settings In this example we’re going to be using https://eeldev.com/auth as our Redirect URL, you can setup your own Web Server to use for this, but you can also continue to use the eelDev host if you wish.

You can use the EOSCoreWeb functions to Authenticate using Epic Accounts to get a Epic Account AccessToken, lets take a look at an example. The first step is to invoke “InitiateEpicAuthentication”, this node will attempt to open a Web Browser for the user so that they can authenticate with their Epic Account, after they’ve authenticated they will be redirected to the “Redirect URI” parameter. In this example you’ll be redirected to the eelDev host where the plugin will attempt to get the Authentication Code returned from Epic. Feel free to use your own web host for the Redirect URL.

After receiving our Authentication Code from the Initiate Epic Authentication function we’re going to use this code to Authenticate with the EOS Web API, see the example below. Note that the AccessToken in this example will not work for creating a RoomToken as that requires a TrustedServer Client. You must use the Connect interface for this.

EOSCore includes the EOSCoreWeb module, Blueprint functions for the EOS Web API. The Web API is a set of HTTP services next to the EOS SDK, used to create voice room tokens, submit player tickets, manage sanctions and more. The module is part of the EOSCore plugin and loads on Win64, Linux, Mac, Android and iOS. There is nothing extra to install or enable. The functions are found under EOSCoreWeb in the Blueprint context menu. Image Image 2

Category Function Use Auth InitiateEpicAuthentication Opens a web browser for Epic Account login and returns the authorization code, see Auth. Not available on mobile Auth RequestAuthAccessToken Exchanges a code, exchange code, refresh token or password for an Epic Account access token Connect RequestAccessToken Requests an access token with client credentials. Needed for Voice, Sanctions and Anti-Cheat Voice CreateRoomToken, RemoveParticipant, ModifyParticipant Creates tokens for players to join a voice room, removes or hard mutes a participant, see Voice Chat (RTC) Ticketing System SubmitTicket Submits a player ticket with the Web API key of your product, see Player Tickets Sanctions CreateSanction, RemoveSanction, QuerySanctions, QuerySanctionsForPlayer, QueryActiveSanctionsForSpecificPlayer Creates, removes and lists sanctions (bans) Sanctions CreateSanctionAppeal, QuerySanctionAppeals, SynchronizeSanctionsToAnExternalService Appeals and sanction sync Anti-Cheat QueryAntiCheatServiceStatusByDeployment Returns the status of the Anti-Cheat service for a deployment Utility GetPublicIp Returns the public IP address of the client, for example for CreateRoomToken

Most functions take an Access Token. Get it from RequestAccessToken with the Client Id and Client Secret of a client in the Developer Portal, under Product Settings > Clients. The client policy decides which Web API features the token can use, for example voice or sanctions. caution The client secret gives access to everything its client policy allows. Functions such as CreateSanction and CreateRoomToken are meant for a dedicated server or a tool you trust, do not ship a client secret with permissions like these in the game client.
Add LogEOSCoreWeb=Verbose to [Core.Log] to log the requests and responses, see Additional Logging.
